mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how a woman becomes married (kiddushin), and how a marriage ends. It also teaches about a yevamah.

chunks.en: A woman becomes married in three ways,
and she becomes free in two ways.
chunks.explain: Free means she is no longer married.

chunks.en: She becomes married with money,
with a document, and with biah, a private way of marrying.

words.note: A private way of getting married.

chunks.en: With money: Beis Shammai say,

words.note: The students of Shammai, a great Sage.

chunks.en: with a dinar or something worth a dinar.

words.note: A silver coin.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,

words.note: The students of Hillel, a great Sage.

chunks.en: with a perutah or something worth a perutah.
chunks.explain: A perutah is a tiny copper coin.

chunks.en: And how much is a perutah?
One eighth of an Italian issar.
chunks.explain: An issar was a small silver coin.

words.note: A small coin.

chunks.he: וְקוֹנָה אֶת עַצְמָהּ בְּגֵט וּבְמִיתַת הַבָּעַל.
chunks.en: And she becomes free with a get, or when her husband dies.

words.note: A document of divorce.

chunks.en: A yevamah becomes the brother's wife only through biah.
chunks.explain: A yevamah is a widow whose husband died with no children.

chunks.he: וְקוֹנָה אֶת עַצְמָהּ בַּחֲלִיצָה וּבְמִיתַת הַיָּבָם:
chunks.en: And she becomes free through chalitzah, or when the brother dies.
chunks.explain: Chalitzah is a ceremony that sets her free from the brother.

words.note: The husband's brother.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how a Jewish servant (eved ivri) is bought and how he goes free. A Jewish maidservant has one more way to go free.

chunks.en: A Jewish servant is bought with money or with a document,
chunks.st: A Hebrew slave can be acquired by his master through money or through a document,

chunks.en: and he goes free after his years,
chunks.explain: He works for six years and then goes free.
chunks.st: and he can acquire himself, i.e., he is emancipated, through years, i.e., when he completes his six years of labor,

chunks.en: or at Yovel, or by paying for the time that is left.
chunks.st: or through the advent of the Jubilee Year, or through the deduction of money.
chunks.stMore: The slave can redeem himself during the six years by paying for his remaining years of slavery.

words.note: The fiftieth year, when servants go free.

chunks.en: A Jewish maidservant has one more way than him:
chunks.st: A Hebrew maidservant has one mode of emancipation more than him,

chunks.en: she goes free when she shows signs of growing up.
chunks.st: as she acquires herself through signs indicating puberty.

words.note: Signs that she is growing up.

chunks.en: A servant whose ear was pierced is bought for longer by the piercing,
chunks.explain: A servant who wants to stay after six years gets his ear pierced.
chunks.st: A slave who is pierced after serving six years is acquired as a slave for a longer period through piercing his ear with an awl,

chunks.he: וְקוֹנֶה אֶת עַצְמוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל וּבְמִיתַת הָאָדוֹן:
chunks.en: and he goes free at Yovel or when the master dies.
chunks.st: and he acquires himself through the advent of the Jubilee Year or through the death of the master.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how a Canaanite servant is bought, and how he can go free. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about it.

chunks.he: עֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי נִקְנֶה בְכֶסֶף וּבִשְׁטָר וּבַחֲזָקָה,
chunks.en: A Canaanite servant is bought with money, with a document, or by taking hold of him.
chunks.st: A Canaanite slave is acquired by means of money, by means of a document, or by means of the master taking possession of him.

words.note: Acting as his owner.

chunks.en: And he can go free with money
chunks.st: And he can acquire himself, i.e., his freedom, by means of money

chunks.en: given by other people,
chunks.st: given by others, i.e., other people can give money to his master,

chunks.en: or with a document that he takes himself.
chunks.st: and by means of a bill of manumission if he accepts it by himself.

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: with money that he gives himself,
chunks.st: The slave can be freed by means of money given by himself,

chunks.en: and with a document that others take for him,
chunks.st: and by means of a bill of manumission if it is accepted by others,

chunks.en: as long as the money belongs to others.
chunks.explain: A servant owns nothing; what he has belongs to his master.
chunks.st: provided that the money he gives belongs to others, not to him. This is because the slave cannot possess property, as anything owned by a slave is considered his master’s.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how animals are bought: a big animal by handing it over, and a small one by lifting it or pulling it.

chunks.en: A big animal is bought by handing it over,
chunks.explain: The owner gives the buyer the reins.
chunks.st: A large domesticated animal is acquired by passing,
chunks.stMore: when its current owner transfers it to a buyer by giving him the reins or the bit.

chunks.en: and a small one by lifting it up.
chunks.st: And a small domesticated animal is acquired by lifting.

chunks.en: This is what Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Eliezer say.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Eliezer.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: a small animal can be bought by pulling it, too.
chunks.st: A small domesticated animal can be acquired by pulling also, and there is no need to lift it.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how land and things that can be moved are bought, and how they can be bought together.

chunks.en: Property that is a guarantee,
chunks.explain: This means land, which cannot be moved.
chunks.st: Property that serves as a guarantee, i.e., land or other items that are fixed in the earth,

chunks.en: is bought with money, with a document, or by taking hold of it.
chunks.st: can be acquired by means of giving money, by means of giving a document, or by means of taking possession of it.

chunks.en: And property that is not a guarantee,
chunks.explain: This means things that can be moved.
chunks.st: Property that does not serve as a guarantee, i.e., movable property,

chunks.en: is bought only by pulling it.
chunks.st: can be acquired only by pulling.

chunks.en: Property that is not a guarantee
chunks.st: Property that does not serve as a guarantee

chunks.he: נִקְנִין עִם נְכָסִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם אַחֲרָיוּת,
chunks.en: can be bought together with property that is a guarantee,
chunks.st: can be acquired along with property that serves as a guarantee

chunks.en: with money, with a document, or by taking hold of it.
chunks.st: by means of giving money, by means of giving a document, or by means of taking possession of them.
chunks.stMore: The movable property is transferred to the buyer’s possession when it is purchased together with the land, by means of an act of acquisition performed on the land. Generally, one is not obligated to take an oath concerning the denial of a claim with regard to land.

chunks.en: And property that is not a guarantee pulls in
chunks.explain: If he must swear about the movable things, he must swear about the land too.
chunks.st: The mishna continues: And in a legal dispute involving both land and movable property, if the defendant makes a partial admission of the claim with regard to the movable property, thereby rendering himself obligated to take an oath denying any responsibility for the remaining property, the movable property

words.note: They pull in.

chunks.en: the property that is a guarantee,
chunks.st: binds the property that serves as a guarantee, i.e., the land,

chunks.en: to swear about it too.
chunks.st: so that he is forced to take an oath concerning the land as well, despite the fact that one is generally not obligated to take an oath for a claim involving land.

mishnayos.summary: When two people trade one thing for another, once one gets his item, the other is responsible for what he is getting. Hekdesh (the Beis HaMikdash) buys things in special ways.

chunks.en: Anything that is used as payment for something else,
chunks.explain: Like trading instead of paying money.
chunks.st: With regard to all items used as monetary value for another item, i.e., instead of a buyer paying money to the seller, they exchange items of value with each other,

chunks.en: once this one gets his thing,
chunks.st: once one party in the transaction acquires the item he is receiving,

chunks.en: the other one is responsible for what he gets in the trade.
chunks.explain: If it gets lost, it is his loss.
chunks.st: this party is obligated with regard to the item being exchanged for it.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, if it is destroyed or lost, he incurs the loss.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הֶחֱלִיף שׁוֹר בְּפָרָה אוֹ חֲמוֹר בְּשׁוֹר,
chunks.en: How so? If he traded an ox for a cow, or a donkey for an ox,
chunks.st: How so? If one exchanges an ox for a cow, or a donkey for an ox,

chunks.en: once this one gets his thing,
chunks.st: once this party acquires the animal that he is receiving,

chunks.en: the other one is responsible for what he gets in the trade.
chunks.st: this party is obligated with regard to the item being exchanged for it.

chunks.en: Hekdesh buys with money,
chunks.explain: Hekdesh means things that belong to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: The authority of the Temple treasury effects acquisition by means of money to the seller.

words.note: Hashem; here, the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and a regular person buys by taking hold.
chunks.st: And the authority, i.e., the mode of acquisition, of a commoner [hedyot] is by possession.

chunks.en: Saying something is for Hashem is like handing it to a regular person.
chunks.explain: Just by saying it, it belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: Furthermore, one’s declaration to the Most High, i.e., when one consecrates an item through speech, is equivalent to transferring an item to a common person, and the item is acquired by the Temple treasury through his mere speech.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna discusses a transaction involving the barter of two items.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches which mitzvos men must do and which mitzvos women must do too.

chunks.en: All the mitzvos a father must do for his son,
chunks.explain: Like teaching him Torah.
chunks.st: With regard to all mitzvot of a son with regard to his father,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains that these are what a father must do for his son.

chunks.en: men must do them and women do not have to.
chunks.st: men are obligated to perform them and women are exempt.

chunks.en: And all the mitzvos a son must do for his father,
chunks.explain: Like honoring his parents.
chunks.st: And with regard to all mitzvot of a father with regard to his son,
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains that this means honoring and fearing parents.

chunks.en: both men and women must do them.
chunks.st: both men and women are obligated to perform them.

chunks.en: And every mitzvah to do that has a set time,
chunks.explain: Like sukkah or shofar.
chunks.st: The mishna notes an additional difference between the obligations of men and women in the performance of mitzvot: With regard to all positive, time-bound mitzvot, i.e., those which must be performed at specific times,

chunks.en: men must do them and women do not have to.
chunks.st: men are obligated to perform them and women are exempt.

chunks.he: וְכָל מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁלֹּא הַזְּמָן גְּרָמָהּ,
chunks.en: And every mitzvah to do that does not have a set time,
chunks.st: And with regard to all positive mitzvot that are not time bound,

chunks.en: both men and women must do them.
chunks.st: both men and women are obligated to perform them.

chunks.en: And every mitzvah of do not do,
chunks.st: And with regard to all prohibitions,

chunks.en: whether it has a set time,
chunks.st: whether they are time-bound

chunks.en: or does not have a set time,
chunks.st: or whether they are not time-bound,

chunks.en: both men and women must keep them,
chunks.st: both men and women are obligated to observe them,

chunks.en: except for: do not destroy the beard, and do not round the head,
chunks.st: except for the prohibitions of: Do not round the corners of your head, and: Do not destroy the corners of your beard,
chunks.stMore: which are derived from the verse: “You shall not round the corners of your head and you shall not destroy the corners of your beard” (Leviticus 19:27),

chunks.en: and the Kohanim's mitzvah not to become tamei to the dead.
chunks.st: and a prohibition that concerns only priests: Do not contract ritual impurity from a corpse (see Leviticus 21:1).
chunks.stMore: These mitzvot apply only to men, not women, despite the fact that they are prohibitions.

mishnayos.summary: Some jobs with korbanos in the Beis HaMikdash are done only by men. Two kinds of women's flour offerings are waved by the women themselves.

chunks.en: Leaning hands on the korban, and waving,
chunks.st: With regard to the placing of hands on the head of an offering, and the waving of certain offerings,

words.note: Leaning hands on the head of a korban.

chunks.en: bringing near, and taking a handful,
chunks.st: and the bringing near of meal-offerings to the corner of the altar, and the removal of a handful from meal-offerings,

words.note: Bringing a flour offering to the corner of the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: burning on the mizbe'ach, and pinching the bird's neck,
chunks.st: and the burning of sacrificial parts on the altar, and the pinching of bird-offerings,

words.note: How a bird korban was done.

chunks.en: sprinkling the blood, and catching the blood,
chunks.st: and the collecting of blood of offerings in a vessel, and the sprinkling of blood,

words.note: Catching the blood of a korban in a bowl.

chunks.en: are done by men and not by women,
chunks.st: these apply to men and not to women.

chunks.en: except for the flour offering of a sotah and of a nezirah,
chunks.explain: A nezirah is a woman who promised not to drink wine.
chunks.st: All these mitzvot apply specifically to men and not to women, except for the meal-offering of a sota, and the meal-offering of a nazirite woman,

words.note: A woman whose husband suspected her and brought her to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: which they wave themselves.
chunks.st: which these women wave.

mishnayos.summary: Mitzvos that depend on the land of Israel are kept only there. Other mitzvos are kept everywhere, except for a few.

chunks.en: Every mitzvah that depends on the land
chunks.st: Any mitzva that is dependent on the land [aretz]

chunks.en: is kept only in Eretz Yisrael.
chunks.explain: Like terumah and ma'aser from crops.
chunks.st: applies only in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: And a mitzvah that does not depend on the land
chunks.st: and any mitzva that is not dependent on the land

chunks.en: is kept both in Eretz Yisrael
chunks.st: applies both in Eretz Yisrael

chunks.en: and outside of Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: and outside of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: except for orlah and kilayim.
chunks.explain: Orlah is fruit of a tree's first three years. Kilayim is mixing kinds of plants.
chunks.st: This is apart from the mitzvot of orla and diverse kinds, which apply even outside of Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: also the new grain.
chunks.explain: New grain may not be eaten until the omer is brought.
chunks.st: This is the halakha even with regard to the prohibition to eat from the new crop before the omer offering has been brought on the sixteenth of Nisan.

words.note: Grain that grew this year.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who does a mitzvah gets good things and the World to Come. Someone who learns Torah and Mishnah and has good ways will not sin quickly.

chunks.en: Whoever does one mitzvah
chunks.st: Anyone who performs one mitzva

chunks.en: gets good things,
chunks.st: has goodness bestowed upon him,

chunks.en: and his days are made long,
chunks.st: his life is lengthened,

chunks.en: and he inherits the land.
chunks.explain: This means the World to Come.
chunks.st: and he inherits the land, i.e., life in the World-to-Come.

chunks.en: And whoever does not do one mitzvah,
chunks.st: And anyone who does not perform one mitzva

chunks.en: does not get good things,
chunks.st: does not have goodness bestowed upon him,

chunks.en: and his days are not made long,
chunks.st: his life is not lengthened,

chunks.en: and he does not inherit the land.
chunks.st: and he does not inherit the land of the World-to-Come.

chunks.he: כָּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בַמִּקְרָא וּבַמִּשְׁנָה וּבְדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ,
chunks.en: Whoever learns Chumash and Mishnah and has good ways,
chunks.explain: Good ways means working and acting nicely.
chunks.st: Anyone who is engaged in the study of Bible, and in the study of Mishna, and in the desired mode of behavior,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he performs labor and generally acts in an appropriate manner,

words.note: The written Torah.
Derech eretz is good, proper behavior.

chunks.en: will not sin quickly,
chunks.st: will not be quick to sin,

chunks.en: as it says (Koheles 4):
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: A rope of three strands does not quickly break.
chunks.st: “And a threefold cord is not quickly broken” (Ecclesiastes 4:12).
chunks.stMore: One who is involved in all three of these activities will not sin easily.

chunks.en: And whoever has no Chumash,
chunks.st: And anyone who does not engage in the study of Bible,

chunks.en: and no Mishnah,
chunks.st: nor the study of Mishna,

chunks.en: and no good ways,
chunks.st: nor the desired mode of behavior,

chunks.en: is not part of the world of people.
chunks.st: is not part of society, i.e., he is not considered a civilized person at all.

mishnayos.summary: A man can make kiddushin himself or through a messenger, and so can a woman. If he gives her several dates, it matters how he says it and how much they are worth.

chunks.en: A man can make kiddushin himself or through his messenger.
chunks.st: A man can betroth a woman by himself or by means of his agent.

chunks.en: A woman can accept kiddushin herself or through her messenger.
chunks.st: Similarly, a woman can become betrothed by herself or by means of her agent.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ כְּשֶׁהִיא נַעֲרָה,
chunks.en: A man can marry off his daughter when she is a young girl,
chunks.explain: A na'arah is a girl just past twelve years old.
chunks.st: A man can betroth his daughter to a man when she is a young woman,

chunks.en: himself or through his messenger.
chunks.st: either by himself or by means of his agent.

chunks.en: If someone says to a woman,
chunks.st: In the case of one who says to a woman:

chunks.en: Become mekudeshes to me with this date,
chunks.explain: Mekudeshes means married to him through kiddushin.
chunks.st: Be betrothed to me with this date,

chunks.en: become mekudeshes to me with this one,
chunks.st: and adds: Be betrothed to me with that one,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה, מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת.
chunks.en: if one of them is worth a perutah, she is married.
chunks.st: then if one of the dates is worth one peruta she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed, since he mentioned betrothal in connection with each date.

chunks.en: With this one, and this one, and this one:
chunks.st: But if he said: Be betrothed to me with this one, and with this one, and with this one,

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה בְּכֻלָּן, מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת.
chunks.en: if all of them together are worth a perutah, she is married.
chunks.st: then even if all of them together are worth one peruta she is betrothed,

chunks.en: And if not, she is not married.
chunks.st: but if not, she is not betrothed.

chunks.en: If she was eating them one at a time,
chunks.st: If he gave her dates with the intention of betrothing her with them, and she was eating them one by one as she received them,

words.note: One by one, as she got them.

chunks.en: she is not married,
chunks.st: she is not betrothed

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בְאַחַת מֵהֶן שָׁוֶה פְרוּטָה:
chunks.en: unless one of them is worth a perutah.
chunks.st: unless one of them is worth one peruta.

mishnayos.summary: If a man gives kiddushin but what he gives, or what he says about himself, turns out different from what he said, she is not married. Rabbi Shimon says if it turned out better, she is married.

chunks.he: הִתְקַדְּשִׁי לִי בְכוֹס זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן,
chunks.en: Become mekudeshes to me with this cup of wine,
chunks.st: If a man said to a woman: Be betrothed to me with this cup of wine,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be honey;
chunks.st: and it was found to be a cup of honey;

chunks.en: or with this cup of honey,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this cup of honey,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be wine;
chunks.st: and it was found to be a cup of wine;

chunks.en: with this silver dinar,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this dinar made of silver,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be gold;
chunks.st: and it was found to be made of gold;

chunks.en: or a gold one,
chunks.st: or if he said: With this dinar made of gold,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be silver;
chunks.st: and it was found to be made of silver;

chunks.en: on condition that I am rich,
chunks.st: or if he said: On the condition that I am wealthy,

chunks.en: and he turned out to be poor;
chunks.st: and he was found to be poor;

chunks.en: or poor, and he turned out to be rich,
chunks.st: or if he said: On the condition that I am poor, and he was found to be wealthy,

chunks.en: she is not married.
chunks.st: she is not betrothed in any of these cases.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: if he fooled her into something better, she is married.
chunks.st: If he misled her to her advantage
chunks.stMore: by giving her something better than what he stated, or if his status was greater than he claimed, she is betrothed.

mishnayos.summary: If a man makes kiddushin on a condition about himself and it turns out false, she is not married, even if she says she wanted him anyway. The same is true if she fooled him.

chunks.en: On condition that I am a Kohen,
chunks.st: If one said to a woman: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a priest,

chunks.en: and he turned out to be a Levi;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a Levite;

chunks.en: or a Levi, and he turned out to be a Kohen;
chunks.st: or if he said: A Levite, and he was found to be a priest;

chunks.en: a nasin, and he turned out to be a mamzer;
chunks.explain: Both of these may not marry most Jews.
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a Gibeonite, a people prohibited by rabbinic law from marrying into the congregation, i.e., from marrying a Jew of fit lineage, and he was found to be a mamzer, who is prohibited by Torah law to marry into the congregation;

words.note: From the Givonim, who were not allowed to marry most Jews.
Someone not allowed to marry most Jews.

chunks.en: or a mamzer, and he turned out to be a nasin;
chunks.st: or he said: A mamzer, and he was found to be a Gibeonite;

chunks.en: one who lives in a town,
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that I am a resident of a small town,

chunks.en: and he turned out to live in a big city;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a resident of a large city;

chunks.en: or in a big city,
chunks.st: or he said: A resident of a city,

chunks.en: and he turned out to live in a town;
chunks.st: and he was found to be a resident of a town;

chunks.en: on condition that my house is near the bathhouse,
chunks.st: or if he said: Be betrothed to me on the condition that my house is close to the bathhouse,

chunks.en: and it turned out to be far;
chunks.st: and it was found to be far;

chunks.en: or far, and it turned out to be near,

chunks.he: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין לֹא מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמַעְלָה,
chunks.en: We do not check past someone who served at the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: With regard to these investigations, one need not investigate from the altar and above.
chunks.stMore: If his ancestors included a priest who served at the altar, one checks no further, as the court would have investigated his lineage before allowing him to participate in the Temple service.

chunks.en: and not past a Levi who sang on the duchan,
chunks.st: Nor do they check from the platform, used by Levites for singing in the Temple, and above,

words.note: The platform where the Leviim sang.

chunks.en: and not past a member of the Sanhedrin.
chunks.st: nor from the Sanhedrin and above,
chunks.stMore: since only one whose lineage has been examined and who was found to be fit can be appointed to the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: And anyone whose fathers were known
chunks.st: And similarly, anyone whose ancestors

chunks.en: as public officers,
chunks.st: held public posts,

chunks.en: or tzedakah collectors,
chunks.st: and anyone whose ancestors were charity collectors,

chunks.en: may marry into Kehunah,
chunks.st: may marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: and there is no need to check them.
chunks.st: and there is no need to investigate their lineage,
chunks.stMore: since no one of flawed lineage would be appointed to those positions.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: also someone who signed as a witness
chunks.st: Even the descendants of one who had signed as a witness

chunks.en: in the old court of Tzippori.
chunks.st: in the old court [ba’arki] of Tzippori do not need to have their lineage investigated.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says:

chunks.en: also someone who was written
chunks.st: Even the descendants of one who was written

chunks.en: in the king's army list.
chunks.st: in the army list [be’isteratya] of the Jewish king do not need to have their lineage investigated.

mishnayos.summary: The daughter of a chalal may never marry a Kohen. It depends on whether the father or the mother was the chalal. Rabbi Yehuda says the same about a ger's daughter.

chunks.en: The daughter of a male chalal
chunks.st: The daughter of a male ḥalal

chunks.en: may never marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: is unfit to marry into the priesthood forever.
chunks.stMore: In other words, all daughters of male descendants of a ḥalal are prohibited from marrying priests, as they have the status of ḥalalot.

chunks.en: A Yisrael who married a chalalah,
chunks.st: If there was an Israelite who married a ḥalala,

words.note: A woman with chalal status.

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: A chalal who married a Yisrael's daughter,
chunks.st: whereas if there was a ḥalal who married a Jewish woman,

chunks.en: his daughter may not marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is unfit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר:
chunks.en: the daughter of a male ger is like the daughter of a male chalal.
chunks.st: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male ḥalal, and she is also prohibited from marrying into the priesthood.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says a girl may marry a Kohen if one of her parents was born Jewish. Rabbi Yosei says even a daughter of two gerim may.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov disagrees and says:

chunks.en: A Yisrael who married a giyores,
chunks.st: If there was an Israelite who married a female convert,

words.note: A woman who joined the Jewish people.

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood,

chunks.en: And a ger who married a Yisrael's daughter,
chunks.st: and similarly if there was a convert who married a Jewish woman,

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: But a ger who married a giyores,
chunks.st: But if there was a male convert who married a female convert,

chunks.en: his daughter may not marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is unfit to marry into the priesthood.

chunks.en: The same for gerim and freed servants,
chunks.st: With regard to both converts and emancipated Canaanite slaves,

chunks.en: even up to ten generations,
chunks.st: their daughters are unfit to marry into the priesthood even up to ten generations.

chunks.en: until the mother is from Yisrael.
chunks.st: This halakha applies to the offspring until his mother is born Jewish.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even a ger who married a giyores,
chunks.st: Even if there was a male convert who married a female convert,

chunks.en: his daughter may marry a Kohen.
chunks.st: his daughter is fit to marry into the priesthood.

mishnayos.summary: A father is not believed to say his son is a mamzer. Rabbi Yehuda says parents are believed about a baby that is not born yet.

chunks.en: If someone says, This son of mine is a mamzer,
chunks.st: One who says: This son of mine is a mamzer,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he claims that the son was born to one forbidden to him by a prohibition that carries the punishment of karet,

chunks.en: he is not believed.
chunks.st: he is not deemed credible to render him a mamzer.

chunks.en: And even if both of them say
chunks.st: And even if both of them, the father and the mother, admit

chunks.en: about the baby she is expecting that it is a mamzer,
chunks.st: that a fetus in her womb is a mamzer,

chunks.en: they are not believed.
chunks.st: they are not deemed credible.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says, they are believed.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: They are deemed credible.

mishnayos.summary: If a father sent a messenger to make kiddushin for his daughter and also did it himself, whichever came first counts. The same is true for a woman and her messenger.

chunks.en: Someone who gave permission to his messenger
chunks.st: In a case of one who authorized his agent

chunks.en: to make kiddushin for his daughter,
chunks.st: to betroth his daughter to a man that the agent would deem fit,

chunks.en: and he himself went and made kiddushin for her,
chunks.st: and the father went and betrothed her to someone else,

chunks.en: if his came first,
chunks.st: if his betrothal preceded that of the agent,

chunks.en: his kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: his betrothal is a valid betrothal;

chunks.en: And if his messenger's came first,
chunks.st: and if the betrothal of his agent preceded his own,

chunks.en: the messenger's kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: the betrothal of the agent is a valid betrothal.

chunks.en: And if it is not known,
chunks.st: And if it is not known whose betrothal came first,

chunks.en: both of them give a get.
chunks.st: both men who might have betrothed her give her a bill of divorce in order to render her permitted to marry someone else.

chunks.en: And if they want,
chunks.st: And if they wish and agree between them,

chunks.en: one gives a get and the other marries her.
chunks.st: one gives a bill of divorce and the other marries her.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּתְנָה רְשׁוּת לִשְׁלוּחָהּ לְקַדְּשָׁהּ,
chunks.en: And the same for a woman who gave permission to her messenger to make kiddushin for her,
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a woman who authorized her agent to betroth her

chunks.en: and she went and made kiddushin herself,
chunks.st: and she then went and betrothed herself to someone else,

chunks.en: if hers came first,
chunks.st: if her own betrothal preceded that of the agent,

chunks.en: her kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: her betrothal is a valid betrothal,

chunks.en: And if her messenger's came first,
chunks.st: and if that of her agent preceded hers,

chunks.en: his kiddushin counts.
chunks.st: the agent’s betrothal is a valid betrothal.

chunks.en: And if it is not known,
chunks.st: And if they do not know whose betrothal came first,

chunks.en: both of them give her a get.
chunks.st: both men who may have betrothed her give her a bill of divorce.

chunks.en: And if they want,
chunks.st: And if they wish,

chunks.he: אֶחָד נוֹתֵן לָהּ גֵּט וְאֶחָד כּוֹנֵס:
chunks.en: one gives her a get and the other marries her.
chunks.st: one may give a bill of divorce and the other marries her.

mishnayos.summary: If a man went far away with his wife and came back with her and children, he does not need to prove who they are. If his wife died there, he must prove only that the children are hers.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁיָּצָא הוּא וְאִשְׁתּוֹ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
chunks.en: Someone who went overseas with his wife,
chunks.st: With regard to one who went overseas with his wife,

chunks.en: and came back with his wife and children,
chunks.st: and returned with his wife and children,

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, אִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּצָאת עִמִּי לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
chunks.en: and said: This woman who went overseas with me,
chunks.st: and said: This is the woman who went overseas with me

chunks.en: here she is, and these are her children,
chunks.st: and these are her children,

chunks.en: he does not need to bring proof,
chunks.st: he is not required to bring proof

chunks.he: לֹא עַל הָאִשָּׁה וְלֹא עַל הַבָּנִים.
chunks.en: not about the woman and not about the children.
chunks.st: with regard to the lineage of the woman, since her lineage was already investigated at the time of their marriage, nor with regard to the lineage of the children.

chunks.en: If she died, and these are her children,
chunks.st: If he returned without the woman and said: My wife died and these are her children,

chunks.en: he brings proof about the children,
chunks.st: he must bring proof that the children were born to his wife,

chunks.en: but he does not bring proof about the woman.
chunks.st: but he does not need to bring proof with regard to the lineage of the woman.

mishnayos.summary: If a man married a woman far away and came back with her and children, he must prove her family is fit. If she died there, he must prove about her and the children.

chunks.en: I married a woman overseas,
chunks.st: If he left when he was unmarried and said upon his return: I married a woman overseas,

chunks.en: and this is she, and these are her children,
chunks.st: and this is she, and these are her children,

chunks.en: he brings proof about the woman,
chunks.st: he must bring proof with regard to the lineage of the woman,

chunks.he: וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה עַל הַבָּנִים.
chunks.en: and he does not need to bring proof about the children.
chunks.st: but he is not required to bring proof with regard to the lineage of the children.

chunks.en: She died, and these are her children,
chunks.st: If he said: I married a woman overseas and she died, and these are her children,

chunks.en: he needs to bring proof
chunks.st: he is required to bring proof

chunks.en: about the woman and about the children.
chunks.st: with regard to both the lineage of the woman and the children.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches the rules of yichud: when a man and a woman may not be alone together, and when it is allowed, like with his own wife, mother, or daughter.

chunks.he: לֹא יִתְיַחֵד אָדָם עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים,
chunks.en: A man may not be alone with two women,
chunks.explain: Being alone together is called yichud.

chunks.en: but one woman may be alone
with two men.
Rabbi Shimon says,

chunks.he: אַף אִישׁ אֶחָד מִתְיַחֵד עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
chunks.en: Even one man may be alone with two women
when his wife is with him,
and he may sleep with them at an inn,
because his wife watches over him.

chunks.he: מִתְיַחֵד אָדָם עִם אִמּוֹ וְעִם בִּתּוֹ,
chunks.en: A man may be alone with his mother and with his daughter,
and sleep close to them.
And when they grow up,

chunks.he: זוֹ יְשֵׁנָה בִכְסוּתָהּ וְזֶה יָשֵׁן בִּכְסוּתוֹ:
chunks.en: she sleeps in her own clothes and he sleeps in his own clothes.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches who should not be a teacher of young children.

chunks.en: A man who is not married should not be a teacher of children,
chunks.st: A bachelor may not act as a teacher of children,

words.note: Literally "scribes": teaching young children.

chunks.en: and a woman should not be a teacher of children.
chunks.st: nor may a woman act as a teacher of children.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: even someone who does not have a wife with him
chunks.st: Even one who does not have a wife

chunks.en: should not be a teacher of children.
chunks.st: may not act as a teacher of children.

mishnayos.summary: The Sages teach which jobs a father should teach his son, and that a living comes from Hashem, not from the job. Rabbi Nehorai says he teaches his son only Torah, which helps a person when young and when old, like Avraham Avinu.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
an unmarried man should not herd animals,

chunks.he: וְלֹא יִישְׁנוּ שְׁנֵי רַוָּקִים בְּטַלִּית אֶחָת.
chunks.en: and two unmarried men should not sleep under one blanket.
But the Sages allow it.
Anyone whose work is with women
should not be alone with women.

chunks.he: וְלֹא יְלַמֵּד אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ אֻמָּנוּת
chunks.en: And a person should not teach his son a job
among women.
Rabbi Meir says,
A person should always teach his son
a clean and easy job,
and daven to the One Who owns all wealth and property,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין אֻמָּנוּת שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ עֲנִיּוּת וַעֲשִׁירוּת,
chunks.en: because there is no job without being poor and being rich.
chunks.explain: Any job can make a person rich or poor.

chunks.en: Being poor does not come from the job,
and being rich does not come from the job,
but everything goes by a person's merit.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says,
Did you ever see a wild animal or a bird
that has a job?
And they get their food without pain.
And they were created only to serve me,
and I was created to serve my Maker.
Is it not right that I should get my food without pain?

words.en: that I will get my food

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שֶׁהֲרֵעוֹתִי מַעֲשַׂי וְקִפַּחְתִּי אֶת פַּרְנָסָתִי.
chunks.en: But I made my deeds bad, and I lost my easy living.
Abba Gurion from Tzadyan
says in the name of Abba Gurya,
A person should not teach his son to be
a donkey driver, a camel driver,
a potter, a sailor,
a shepherd, or a storekeeper,
because their jobs are the jobs of robbers.
chunks.explain: These jobs can easily lead to taking what is not yours.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says in his name,
Most donkey drivers are wicked,
and most camel drivers are good people.
chunks.explain: They travel in dangerous places and daven to Hashem.

chunks.en: Most sailors are pious.
chunks.explain: The danger of the sea makes them fear Hashem.

chunks.en: The best of doctors goes to Gehinnom.
And the most kosher of butchers
is a partner of Amalek.
Rabbi Nehorai says,
I put aside every job in the world,

chunks.he: וְאֵינִי מְלַמֵּד אֶת בְּנִי אֶלָּא תוֹרָה,
chunks.en: and I teach my son only Torah,
because a person eats from its reward in this world,
and the main reward stays for the World to Come.
And all other jobs are not like that.
When a person becomes sick,
or old,
or has suffering,
and he cannot do his work,
he dies of hunger.
But Torah is not like that.
chunks.explain: A person can learn Torah at any time.

chunks.en: It guards him from all bad when he is young,
and gives him a future and hope when he is old.
About his youth, what does it say?
(Yeshayahu 40) Those who hope to Hashem will have new strength.
About his old age, what does it say?
(Tehillim 92) They will still give fruit in old age.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
chunks.en: And so it says about Avraham Avinu, may he rest in peace,
(Bereishis 24) And Avraham was old,
and Hashem blessed Avraham with everything.
We find that Avraham Avinu kept

chunks.he: אֶת כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנָה,
chunks.en: the whole Torah before it was given,

chunks.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, (שם כו) עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם
chunks.en: as it says (there 26): Because Avraham listened

chunks.he: בְּקֹלִי וַיִּשְׁמֹר מִשְׁמַרְתִּי מִצְוֹתַי חֻקּוֹתַי וְתוֹרֹתָי:
chunks.en: to My voice, and kept My watch, My mitzvos, My laws, and My teachings.
